engine_audit.corrected_line: Every Barbarian runs on Energy; Enrage unlocks its gated attacks and cuts global cooldowns by 30%.
evidence: structural:barbarian:barb-chassis-energy — 'Hodir's Wrath restores 100% of maximum Energy, establishing Energy as a shared Barbarian resource.' The bar named in the blurb is right, and it is genuinely shared: all three spec claim sets spend and refill Energy.

structural:barbarian:barb-chassis-enrage — 'Bloodthirsty Rage can trigger Enrage from melee auto attacks, and Enrage reduces Barbarian ability global cooldowns.' This is the ONLY part of Enrage the blurb carries, and it is the smaller half.

The weighting miss: Enrage is a hard gate, not just a speed buff. Digest shows 'Requires Enraged' on Smash (spell:barbarian:801755), Outrage (spell:barbarian:801759), Ancestral Roar (spell:barbarian:500918), Berserker Axe (talent:barbarian/headhunting:12-32-4-0), and 'Only usable while Enraged' on Rampage (spell:barbarian:801786).

The gate reaches the resource itself. structural:barbarian/brutality:brutality-energy-execute — 'Thirst for Battle makes Smash restore 25% maximum Energy' — and Smash Requires Enraged. Brutality's largest sustained refill is therefore behind the Enrage gate, which 'speeds the whole kit up' does not convey.

structural:barbarian/headhunting:headhunting-reset-charges — 'You Want Axe? makes Spears cast while Enraged refresh three Berserker Axe charges with reduced Energy cost.' Headhunting's whole payoff window is keyed to Enrage, not to a haste effect.

Enrage effects also FEED Energy rather than only accelerating it: Onslaught (spell:barbarian:801758) 'Become enraged, instantly generating 25 Energy plus an additional 20 Energy every 2 sec for 10 sec'; Ancestral Might (spell:barbarian:801789) reduces Physical ability Energy cost by 25% while enraged.

Not a Chronomancer-style miss: the blurb names the correct engine. The correction is one of weighting — Enrage is the switch that opens abilities and the Energy taps, and the 30% figure (digest: Barbaric Rage, on Bloodthirsty Rage and Ancestral Might) makes that concrete.

flags: CONTRADICTION with landed site copy: the Brutality roster entry says the spec 'builds Fury through crushing swings and Whirls' and its coreLoop says 'build momentum and Fury'. No claim and no digest entry defines a resource called Fury. A regex over all 299 digest talents and skills found zero instances of gaining, generating, building, spending, or consuming Fury; the word appears only inside talent NAMES (Steel Fury, Deep Fury, Mounting Fury, Ancestral Fury, Frost Giant's Fury, Voodoo Fury, Ancestor's Fury, Fury of the North). The real resource is Energy. Recommend the class page not inherit that phrasing, and that the roster line be raised as a separate correction.

The Brutality roster entry also carries an empty resources array ("resources":[]) while claim structural:barbarian:barb-chassis-energy and five Brutality talents establish Energy. The site data understates the engine for this spec.

Claim barb-chassis-energy's own limitation reads 'This locator establishes restoration, not the costs of each ability.' My engine body therefore says Energy 'pays for Barbarian abilities' generally and never asserts that every ability costs Energy. Several digest talents remove Energy costs outright (Smasher, Broken Bones, Raging Spirit on Spirit spells), so a blanket cost claim would be false.

The 30% global-cooldown figure is digest-only (Barbaric Rage, attached to Bloodthirsty Rage and Ancestral Might). Claim barb-chassis-enrage states the reduction without a number, and its limitation notes 'The proc chance and duration belong to this specific Enrage source' — so the 10% proc chance and 8-second Enrage duration are NOT class-wide and I excluded them.

Ancestry Tankard stack CAP is unknown. Claim ancestry-fill-spend's limitation says 'The precise stack count and chosen supporting talents can change the cadence', so no maximum Fill Level is stated anywhere I could reach. The vessel topology and all Ancestry copy deliberately avoid naming a cap.

The vessel topology is talent-dependent. Digest talent The Finest Ale (talent:barbarian/ancestry:12-33-8-4) reads 'Your Ale of The God-King no longer empties your Tankard' — one talent removes the emptying for that ability, though Breath of The North and Splash Zone still key off emptying. The seal and strip should not present emptying as unconditional.

Claim ancestry-ancestor's limitation notes the Ancestor's Call description is truncated after its mimic condition. I used the pet only as an attention object in the eyes line and never described its full behavior.

The two Brutality player_experience claims conflict with each other — brutality-leveling-concern reports single-enemy recovery pressure in the 50s, brutality-leveling-counterreport describes multi-enemy pulls tied to cooldowns, both from the same thread (reddit:def112822a19), neither documenting talents, level, or gear. Nothing in my proposals rests on either.

Claim headhunting-player-cooldown-observation carries the explicit limitation 'this observation is not used for mechanics or fit'. I honored that: the Headhunting wheel topology rests on the two structural claims plus digest, not on the player report, even though the report happens to describe the same rhythm.

QUARANTINE CHECK: clean. Nothing proposed here touches enjoy_avoid_fit or role_range for any spec, and Barbarian is not one of the six quarantined specs (chronomancer, artificer, runemaster, riftblade, starcaller, moon-priest). Barbarian's landed roles (Damage, Damage, Support) and ranges (Melee, Ranged, Melee) are used only as page framing, never as evidence for a proposal.

engine_audit.engine_name: Rage as the shared bar, health as the second cost, under a Blood Curse / Cursed Form switch
evidence: The landed blurb reads: 'The spells cost blood; spent health returns as Thirst and Rage.' Thirst is NOT class-wide. Its only claim is structural:bloodmage/sanguine:c-sanguine-thirst ('Health-cost spells grant Thirst; at ten stacks the specialization becomes Insatiable'), and the seemingly class-level claim structural:bloodmage:c-class-thirst-rage locates to spell:bloodmage:500107 — the same Sanguine level-10 passive surfacing in the class skill table. This is the Chronomancer failure exactly: a cited line promoting one spec's meter to the class engine.

Health-cost spells pay out DIFFERENTLY per spec, so 'returns as Thirst' is wrong for three of four. Fleshweaver: structural:bloodmage/fleshweaver:c-fleshweaver-pooled-vitality — 'Health-cost spells grant Pooled Vitality stacks, and Rage-cost Mortal Form spells consume ten stacks to become empowered.' Eternal: structural:bloodmage/eternal:c-eternal-curse — health-cost spell damage feeds THREAT, not a stack. Accursed's counter is not health-fed at all: structural:bloodmage/accursed:c-accursed-shards — 'Shadow damage generates Blood Shards up to eight.'

Rage is the actual shared bar, and the blurb buries it in third position. structural:bloodmage:c-class-health-rage (Rage-cost abilities consume health for added value) · structural:bloodmage/eternal:c-eternal-rage ('increases Rage from damage') · structural:bloodmage/eternal:c-eternal-rotclaw ('generates Rage') · structural:bloodmage/fleshweaver:c-fleshweaver-hemoglobe ('generates Pooled Vitality plus Rage') · structural:bloodmage/fleshweaver:c-fleshweaver-pooled-vitality ('Rage-cost Mortal Form spells') · structural:bloodmage/sanguine:c-sanguine-thirst ('the Thirst effect also generates Rage') · observed:bloodmage/sanguine:o-sanguine-change-history (a prior change to 'Vampiric Fang's Rage cost').

The blurb omits the one structure every spec claims: Blood Curse converts into a per-spec Cursed Form, and the kit splits into Mortal Form and Cursed Form halves. structural:bloodmage/accursed:c-accursed-form ('Accursed Form replaces Blood Curse with a Cursed Form') · structural:bloodmage/eternal:c-eternal-curse ('Eternal Curse is a Cursed Form') · structural:bloodmage/sanguine:c-sanguine-transgression ('Transgression is a Cursed Form that does not disable Mortal Form abilities') · structural:bloodmage/fleshweaver:c-fleshweaver-dark-essence ('Cursed Form abilities or Bloodbolt heal allies') · structural:bloodmage/accursed:c-accursed-mobile ('Unchained permits damaging Mortal Form spells to be cast while moving') · structural:bloodmage/accursed:c-accursed-aortic ('extends an active Cursed Form').

Pattern class: nearest to Witch Hunter (one shared bar with per-spec layers) but with a second axis no landed class has — a form switch. Rage is shared; health is a cost paid on top; each spec layers its own counter (Thirst 10 / Pooled Vitality 10 / Blood Shards 8, Eternal none); and Blood Curse becomes four different Cursed Forms that re-gate the kit.
engine_audit.corrected_line: Every Bloodmage runs on Rage with health as the second cost; each spec turns Blood Curse into its own Cursed Form.

seal_concept.geometry_idea: A two-chambered heart sits at the center, drawn as one continuous vein that loops back into itself — the Mortal chamber left hollow, the Cursed chamber filled solid, so the form switch reads before any label does. Four vessels leave the heart, one per spec, and each is beaded with the counter that spec actually fills: ten beads for Thirst, ten for Pooled Vitality, eight for Blood Shards. Eternal's vessel carries no beads and is drawn thick and blunt instead, because its payout is threat rather than a stack — the one artery that never counts.
seal_concept.node_extras: Sanguine's tenth bead is drawn as an open ring rather than a filled dot, marking Insatiable at the cap (structural:bloodmage/sanguine:c-sanguine-thirst). Accursed's vessel carries a short arc segment for the 30-second form with a small notch where Aortic Assault pushes it forward (structural:bloodmage/accursed:c-accursed-aortic). Fleshweaver's tenth bead branches out into small ally dots, since its cash-out is what empowers the spell that reaches the group (structural:bloodmage/fleshweaver:c-fleshweaver-pooled-vitality).
seal_concept.legend: Beads count the stack that must fill before the cash-out — 10 Thirst, 10 Pooled Vitality, 8 Blood Shards. A filled chamber means Cursed Form; a hollow one means Mortal Form.

flags: ENGINE CORRECTION (primary): the landed blurb promotes Thirst to a class-wide return. Thirst is claimed only for Sanguine, and the apparently class-level claim structural:bloodmage:c-class-thirst-rage locates to spell:bloodmage:500107 — the Sanguine level-10 passive appearing in the class skill table. Fleshweaver's health-cost payout is Pooled Vitality; Eternal's is threat; Accursed's counter is fed by Shadow damage, not health. Treat this as the same failure mode as Chronomancer.

ACCURSED HAS NO RAGE OR HEALTH-COST CLAIM. All four Accursed claims (form, aortic, mobile, shards) are silent on Rage and on health costs. The 'Rage is shared by every spec' derivation rests on three claimed specs plus the class node, plus digest-only support for Accursed (Killer Instinct: Rage raises Veinburst/Reave crit; Puncturing Fangs: +3 Rage per Bloodmoon Blast hit; Blood Pact: +20 max Rage; Gore Barrage: -30% cost on health-cost spells). Digest-backed, not claim-backed, for that one spec.

DIGEST CONTRADICTION — Insatiable tick rate: talent:bloodmage/sanguine:20-26-10-0 says '-30% every 3 sec'; spell:bloodmage:500107 says '30% every 1.50 sec'. I used the -30% magnitude (consistent in both) and deliberately omitted the interval. Do not print a tick interval until this resolves.

DIGEST CONTRADICTION — Aortic Assault cadence: talent:bloodmage/accursed:20-52-7-3 says 'every 1 sec for 3 seconds'; spell:bloodmage:806212 says 'every 0.5 sec for 3 sec'. The +3 sec Cursed Form extension agrees in both, so only the extension is used.

TRUNCATED DIGEST STRINGS. Thirst's escalating-cost text, Accursed Form, Transgression, Sanguine Essence, Blood Shards damage, and Dark Liturgy's Blood Rituals text all cut off mid-sentence (the claims themselves note this). The Sanguine bullet says 'raises the health price' with no number precisely because the '+5% per stack' figure sits inside a truncated string.

INFERENCE, NOT A CLAIM: that Cursed Form normally disables Mortal Form spells. No claim states the rule; it is inferred from two claims naming exceptions (structural:bloodmage/sanguine:c-sanguine-transgression and Sanguine Essence both 'do not disable Mortal Form abilities') plus the digest's 'Requires Mortal Form' / 'Requires Cursed Form' gating on individual spells. The engine body is worded to avoid asserting the rule ('your kit splits into Mortal Form spells and Cursed Form abilities').

TWO NEW TOPOLOGY FAMILIES PROPOSED — 'bank-overrun' (Sanguine) and 'window-stretch' (Accursed). Neither is in the landed set. If the design lead prefers not to grow the vocabulary, Sanguine maps to 'bank' and Accursed to 'wave', at the cost of losing the Insatiable penalty and the self-extending window respectively.
'Overdraw' is a coinage, not an in-game term. It was chosen over 'Gorge' and 'Sate' because both collide with real names (the Fleshweaver talent Gorge, the Sanguine buff Sated).

ALTERNATIVE TENSION LINE considered and set aside: 'MORTAL · CAST / CURSED · FORM'. It encodes the form fork instead of the health-for-Rage trade. Rejected because 'CURSED · CLAW' phrasing over-generalizes (Transgression and Sanguine Essence keep Mortal Form abilities live), and the geometry already carries the fork via the filled/hollow chambers.

ETERNAL HAS NO STACK COUNTER in any claim — the seal draws its vessel unbeaded on that basis. This is an argument from claim silence, not a positive claim that no counter exists. Verify before it ships as a visual assertion.

engine_audit.engine_name: No shared engine — three per-spec clocks, each cashed for seconds (shorter casts or longer windows), over a shared support chassis of party healing plus one personal Rewind.
evidence: Derivation, not the blurb: the three structural spec claims name three DIFFERENT meters and no common resource. structural:chronomancer/artificer:c-art-fragment-engine = Echo Fragments ('Wand of Time creates Echo Fragments for Distortion and Continuum spells; Fragment spending increases Shatter Echo damage, and Continuum effects can gain duration from spent Fragments').

structural:chronomancer/infinite:c-inf-periodic-engine = a periodic-damage clock ('Melt Reality deals recurring target damage that replicates nearby, while periodic damage can trigger Anomaly Spikes that reduce Chromatic Shard's cast time'). No resource bar is named anywhere in the Infinite claims.

structural:chronomancer/time:c-time-aeon-engine = the Aeon/Epoch clock ('Aeon of Resilience and Aeon of Protection change Epoch, and Epoch grants Endless Sands that reduces the cast time of later Reverse Wounds').

The two class-level claims are both SHARED UTILITY, not a resource: structural:chronomancer:c-chassis-rewind ('Timewalking stores health, mana, and location in an Infinite Clone that Rewind can return to') and structural:chronomancer:c-chassis-timeline ('Fortify Timeline instantly heals party members and extends Accelerated Recovery, a periodic heal'). Neither is generated, spent, or consumed — so neither is an engine.

Cross-check in the shared talent tree (digest, target 'chronomancer', 39 nodes): every node is utility, healing, control, or a flat stat. Not one node generates, spends, or gates on a class resource. This is the Guardian 'no shared engine' pattern, minus even a shared floor resource.

The through-line the three clocks DO share is the payoff currency, time: Endless Sands cuts 20% per stack off the next Reverse Wounds; Anomaly Spike stacks cut 10% per stack off Chromatic Shard; a consumed Echo Fragment adds 5 sec to a Continuum spell.

Blurb comparison — current ENGINES.Chronomancer p = 'Each spec runs its own clock — DoT ramps, Echo Fragments, or Aeons — and Rewind is just the safety net.' It names the correct engine (three per-spec clocks, no shared bar), names each clock correctly, and correctly DEMOTES the shared layer. Verdict confirmed; the earlier shared-utility-led version is the one that was wrong.

Weighting caveat (non-blocking, logged as a flag, not a correction): the blurb's second half names only Rewind and drops c-chassis-timeline, the other half of the shared chassis (party heal + a 5 sec Accelerated Recovery extension).

engine_audit.engine_name: One shared spend-bar (Runic Power) under per-spec layers, with every spec's payoff triggered by Command spells, plus Life Force as a second, non-cycling roster budget. This is the Witch Hunter shape (one shared bar under per-spec layers) with a standing allocation pool bolted on, not a Life Force engine.
evidence: structural:necromancer:c-runic-command — 'Crypt Swarm and Flesh to Worms generate Runic Power, while Command spells have Runic Power costs.' This is the only claim describing a generate/spend cycle. Runic Power is the bar that moves.

structural:necromancer:c-life-force — 'Necromancy lets the class summon undead using Life Force, and summoned minion scaling is tied to the Life Force used.' Life Force is occupancy, not expenditure: minions 'occupy' 1/2/3 Life Force for as long as they stand. Nothing in the claims or digest generates Life Force back during combat; the only Life Force numbers in the corpus are +1 capacity passives (Summoning Adept, Summoning Expert, Master Animator). A pool that never cycles is a budget, not an engine.

All three specs hang their signature layer on the Command cast, not on Life Force. Animation: structural:necromancer/animation:a-command-cycle — 'Animation Commands can make another Command free, make Lichfrost or Blight free and instant, and reduce Animate cooldowns.' Death: structural:necromancer/death:d-engine — 'makes Commands apply Expunge to diseased enemies', and d-spread — 'Crypt Explosion applies Crypt Plague near the primary target' (Commands). Rime: structural:necromancer/rime:r-runic-cycle — 'Commands can reset and free Ice Barrage; and Glacial Impact can generate 20 Runic Power.'

structural:necromancer:c-stances — 'Command abilities shown in the digest cannot be used during Pacify.' The one shared class-wide gate in the corpus gates Commands, not summoning. Losing Commands turns off all three spec engines.

Rime is the tell that the bar closes a loop: Freeze Dry (talent:necromancer/rime:23-60-7-3b) puts 20 Runic Power back in, and Lich Commander (talent:necromancer:23-87-3-6b) takes 5 off every Command's cost. Both nodes exist to keep Commands flowing. No comparable node exists to refill Life Force.

Blurb weighting problem: the landed label reads 'The engine — Life Force' and the body reads 'Life Force raises your undead; Runic Power gives them their orders.' Both clauses are individually true, but the label names the static pool as THE engine and the sentence demotes the actual cycling bar to a supporting clause. This is the Chronomancer failure mode: a cited line naming the wrong primary.

RIGHT ENGINE, WRONG WEIGHTING — the name 'Advantage' is correct and the build source is correct. structural:ranger:c-chassis-cycle: 'Quick Shot and Wild Strike each generate Advantage, Precision Shot gains damage per Advantage stack, and Readiness generates Focus every five seconds.' Digest confirms both builders are 'Generates 1 Advantage' (spell:ranger:500074, spell:ranger:501724).

SPEND IS CONFIRMED, not inferred. Five independent tooltips name consumption: Ranger General's Command 'Consumes Advantage' (spell:ranger:803118); Sniper's Focus 'Consuming Advantage' (talent:ranger/archery:21-54-10-2); Thread The Needle 'your next ability that consumes Advantage' (talent:ranger/farstrider:21-2-4-7); Rub It In 'Each stack of Advantage spent' (spell:ranger:705085); Elven Tactics 'chance to not consume Advantage on cast' (talent:ranger:21-87-6-6 area).

ERROR 1 — 'finishers' is the wrong frame. The overwhelming majority of Advantage spenders are core rotational abilities usable at any target health: Precision Shot (spell:ranger:500075), Skullpiercer (spell:ranger:802036), Woodland Arrow (spell:ranger:806368), Emerald Arrow (talent:ranger/farstrider:21-2-5-4b), Quills (talent:ranger/brigand:21-55-4-6), Serrated Shot (spell:ranger:500073), Skirmish (spell:ranger:802039). Only Deadshot (below 20% health) and Assault (low health only) are execute-gated. 'Finishers' imports a combo-point frame that fits two abilities out of nine.

ERROR 2 — 'scaled' hides that the scaled axis is duration as often as damage. Skirmish 'Lasts 4 sec for each stack of Advantage'; Serrated Shot 'Duration increased by 4 sec per stack'; Neurotoxin Arrow 'Duration increased by 1 sec per stack'; Dirty Blades 'Duration increased by 4 s per stack'; Ranger General's Command 'Duration increased for each stack of Advantage exhausted'. Archery's central payoff is a WINDOW whose length the stacks buy, not a bigger hit.

ERROR 3 — the five-stack threshold economy is absent from the blurb entirely, and it is the class's distinguishing shape (the Knight-of-Xoroth analogue at 5 instead of 6). 'used with 5 stacks of Advantage' / 'spending 5 stacks of Advantage at once' appears nine times in the digest: Phoenix Plumes (spell:ranger:705074), Whipping Pressure (spell:ranger:705100), Forest Fighter (spell:ranger:706282), Maximum Power (talent:ranger/archery:21-54-4-5), Stonemason's Secret (talent:ranger/brigand:21-55-6-8), Farstrider Ranger (spell:ranger:800243).

CEILING = 5, inferred but strong: Guise 'Instantly generates 5 stacks of Advantage' reads as a full-charge button (talent:ranger:21-87-6-6b), and Farstrider Ranger says 'spending 5 stacks of Advantage at once'. No tooltip states a literal cap; flagged.

NOT the Witch Hunter shape (one shared bar under per-spec layers) and NOT the Guardian shape (no shared engine). This is one resource with a threshold economy — same family as Knight of Xoroth's six-stack Demonfire — but with a second scaling axis (duration) that Demonfire does not have.

engine_audit.engine_name: The soul ladder - one shared three-rung conversion ladder (Soul Fragment to Reaped Soul to Soul Infusion), where the middle and top rungs are both separately spendable
evidence: structural:reaper:c1 states it outright: 'the class ladder converts three Soul Fragments into a Reaped Soul and three Reaped Souls into Soul Infusion.' The blurb is a near-literal restatement, so the named engine is the claimed engine.

Digest Soul Collector (spell:reaper:706731) is the class passive that IS the engine: 'Your Reap generates 1 Soul Fragment. Generating 3 Soul Fragments generates a Reaped Soul. Generating 3 Reaped Souls generates a Soul Infusion, which allows the use of powerful abilties.' No competing class-wide resource passive exists in the digest.

Weighting check - all three spec structural claims are ladder claims, so 'every Reaper climbs the same ladder' carries the right weight. Domination (structural:reaper/domination:c3): 'Dreadwake generates a Reaped Soul; reaching three souls grants temporary physical-damage reduction and health recovery, while Spectral Scythe consumes Reaped Souls and Soul Infusion.'

Harvest (structural:reaper/harvest:c5 and c6): 'Slaughter grants a Reaped Soul but normally requires a target below 35% health'; 'Crow's Harvest strikes nearby enemies and harvests Soul Fragments from damage, up to three.' Soul (structural:reaper/soul:c8): 'Dirge generates two Soul Fragments; Endbringer gives Dirge a timed damage-and-range increase, three Reaped Souls, and healing from damage.'

This is a NEW engine pattern, distinct from the three seen so far. Not Witch Hunter's one shared bar (the Reaper resource changes identity as it converts), not Guardian's no-shared-engine (all three specs feed one class passive), and not Knight of Xoroth's single resource with one threshold (Reaper has two conversion thresholds, and the middle rung is a spend target in its own right).

Where the blurb is thin but not wrong: structural:reaper:c1 names a second resource in the same sentence ('Reap generates one Soul Fragment and Runic Power') that the blurb omits, and structural:reaper/domination:c3 shows the middle rung paying out on its own (3 souls held) and being consumed on its own (Spectral Scythe). Both are body-draft material, not a correction - the blurb still names the right engine.

engine_audit.engine_name: Weapon Engravings — a shared trigger-chance layer under three unrelated per-spec counters (no shared bar or stack)
evidence: structural:runemaster:c-chassis-engraving-window is the ONLY class-level structural claim, and it names a chance economy, not a write/release loop: 'Runic Tattoos reduce resource costs, and Zenith raises Weapon Engraving trigger chance by 100% for six seconds.' Engravings are never written and never released — they land on a chance you buy up.

structural:runemaster/riftblade:r-riftblade-cycle has NO write step at all: 'every third Runeblade has both a counted damage effect and a transformed next-cast effect.' The blurb's three-item list (engravings / glyphs / brands) omits Riftblade's actual engine entirely.
structural:runemaster/arcane:a-arcane-cycle does fit write-then-release: Frost -> Flame -> Arcane, 'and Glyphic Ruin unleashes the active Glyph.'
structural:runemaster/runic:u-runic-cycle also fits: 'Runic Brand marks an enemy so the next Runeblade causes a Runic Explosion.'

No shared bar or stack exists across the three specs. Runeblade charges appear only in Runic (u-runic-cycle: 'Primordial Blast restores three Runeblade charges') and Riftblade (r-riftblade-cycle: 'Primordial Blast and Smolder refresh Runeblade charges'); Arcane runs Glyphs instead. The only thing all three touch is the Engraving layer (Runic's Fist of the Ancients 'triggers a Weapon Engraving' per u-runic-cycle; the class tree's Decoder/Master Engraver/Convergence sit on it).

So the blurb is right to say 'engravings' in the label but wrong in weighting: it frames the class as write-then-release when the shared layer is a proc-chance economy, and the write/release frame covers only two of the three specs.

engine_audit.engine_name: Scattered Stars — one shared resource that does not sit on the player. It is a stacking mark planted on enemies (cap 4, 30 sec) and consumed back for refunds: cooldown, mana, healing, or a free strike. Not 'one shared bar' (Witch Hunter), not 'no shared engine' (Guardian), not a single threshold economy (Knight of Xoroth). Its distinguishing shape is that the resource is externalized onto targets, so building it and reaching it are the same problem, and consumption is a refund loop rather than a terminal spend.
evidence: structural:starcaller:c-chassis-stars — 'Cycle of the Moon can apply Scattered Stars during New Moon, Aspect of the Stars can apply them from auto attacks, Lunar Lance consumes them for additional damage and mana return, and Starcall both applies stars and gains cooldown reduction when one is consumed.' Establishes the class chassis as apply+consume on one named resource.

All four spec claims independently run the same apply/consume pair, so the blurb's 'every spec' is not overreach: c-mg-cycle (Starburst applies per hit / Starsweep consumes), c-mp-engine (Huntress Shot applies 2 extra / Moonflow consumes), c-sen-cycle (Starcall applies / Starfire Shot consumes), c-war-cycle (Starsunder crit and Fan of Knives apply / Umbral Blade consumes).

Payoff really is per-spec, which is the blurb's second half: Moon Guard gets cooldown off Starsweep (c-mg-cycle), Moon Priest gets a heal on up to 5 allies (c-mp-engine), Sentinel gets mana and a Starcall improvement (c-sen-cycle), Warden gets a free Astral Blade (c-war-cycle).

Chronomancer check applied: no spec's loop runs on a different named resource. There is no competing meter in any of the four structural spec claims — every spec-defining node in those claims names Scattered Stars.

Weighting caveat (does not change the verdict): the claims show consumption is dominantly a refund that feeds re-application — Starcall loses 1.5 sec per star consumed, Starsweep 3 sec, Fan of Knives 2 sec, Lunar Lance and Starfire Shot return 8% maximum mana per star. Weighting check on the first clause: giving Solar Power co-billing is defensible because the authoritative claim gives it co-billing, and because Valkyrie's level-10 capstone is built on generating it — "Auto attacks generate 1 Solar Power" (talent:sun-cleric/valkyrie:27-90-10-6). Digest spell:templar:801443 Righteous Lunge — '...granting an Oath. Oath: Your abilities damage or heal for 10% more.' An Oath is a live buff while held, not inert fuel. THE SIX-VENOM COUNT IS MY ENUMERATION, NOT A CLAIMED NUMBER. The digest yields six distinct Venoms (Rejuvenating, Debilitating, Adrenal, Blight, Nullifying, Weakening); no claim states a total. I kept "six" out of the engine body and out of the seal legend for this reason. Verify against the roster before any surface prints it.

WEAVER FORM AND VIZIER FORM ARE LOCATOR-BACKED, NOT TEXT-BACKED. Neither is named in any claim's text; both appear only as locators inside c-venom-cycle (talent:venomancer/venom:29-76-10-4) and c-vizier-cycle (talent:venomancer/vizier:29-92-10-4). Beetle Form and Spider Form are named in claim text (c-fortitude-role, c-stalking-range). The seal's four-form geometry therefore rests on two named forms plus two locator-derived ones — solid, but note the asymmetry if the seal ships form names as visible labels.

FORTITUDE'S "15 SEC AT FULL" IS DERIVED ARITHMETIC, NOT A STATED NUMBER: 5 sec base + 1 sec per stack (29-78-4-3) × 10 max stacks (29-78-10-0). Also derived and NOT used anywhere above: 10 stacks × 3% = +30% physical damage taken at full. Both are safe multiplications of two claim-cited facts, but neither is written down as such.

QUARANTINE PROXIMITY — LOW BUT NON-ZERO. No quarantined pair involves Venomancer. However c-stalking-range (Serpent Lord's +10 yds on some Spider Form abilities) is range-shaped evidence, and the claim's own limitation says the range "belongs to an optional Serpent Lord branch and affects only some Spider Form abilities." I confined it to one Stalking bullet, framed as optional, and kept it out of the engine, the verb, and the seal. Do not let it drift into any role/range framing.

VIZIER BULLET 3 LEANS ON A SINGLE PLAYER REPORT. "one player reported it out-healed most of their other heals" traces to observed:venomancer/vizier:o-vizier-output-concern, whose own limitation is "no build, combat log, or evidence that later changes had not altered its outcome." I attributed it explicitly rather than stating it as fact. It is the weakest line in the packet — drop it and Vizier still has two solid bullets.

EVIDENCE I DELIBERATELY LEFT UNUSED, so it does not resurface as a gap: observed:venomancer/stalking:o-stalking-fight-length (one level-45 report on ~30-second fights and limited area damage — too thin, and it reads as a balance verdict); observed:venomancer/venom:o-venom-ease (one comment grouping Venom as new-player-accessible — no build or level band); observed:venomancer/vizier:o-vizier-sufficiency (a comment about judging healing by deaths, not a mechanic); observed:venomancer/fortitude:o-fortitude-practice (advises restraint on Carapace Regeneration — I did not build a bullet on it because Carapace Regeneration's 10-Rage-per-tick drain is digest-only and the guide is one unsourced post).

TWO NEW TOPOLOGY FAMILIES PROPOSED, both under the task's "name a new one and describe it" allowance: "debt-bank" (Fortitude) and "countdown-bank" (Vizier). Neither fits the existing seven cleanly — Fortitude's bar fills against your will and taxes you while held, and Vizier's two counters deplete rather than climb. If the design pass would rather not mint families, Fortitude degrades to "bank" and Vizier to "bank" with the distinction carried in window_sub, at some loss of accuracy.

evidence: structural:witch-doctor:c-chassis-shared — 'The shared kit can collect Spirits that regenerate health and mana...' The class-level claim names Spirits, so the engine NAME in the blurb is right; only the weighting is wrong.

structural:witch-doctor/shadowhunting:c-shadow-engine — 'Reclamation is usable while moving and collects a Spirit; active Spirits can produce additional Reclamation casts and Spirit Eclipse unleashes active Spirits.' For Shadowhunting the Spirit stack IS the spec economy, not a layer underneath a separate one — which is exactly what 'each spec runs its own economy on top' denies.

structural:witch-doctor/shadowhunting:c-shadow-tracking — 'Spirit collection and Voodoo Hunger stack growth give Shadowhunting two changing values that can determine an Eclipse or Malefic Arrow payoff.' The claim makes the Spirit count a payoff determinant, not a sustain readout.

structural:witch-doctor/voodoo:c-voodoo-rhythm — 'Voodoo can collect Spirits from damage or Shadow Puppets, and Hexfire can snap Puppeteer's Threads for stored damage while collecting a Spirit.' Voodoo collects on the same bar; Threads sit beside it, not instead of it.
structural:witch-doctor/voodoo:c-voodoo-role — 'Bad Juju is a Spirit-scaling spell with a Hex of Malice condition.' Payoff scales off Spirit.

digest Loa Spirits (talent:witch-doctor/voodoo:13-34-3-1) — 'stacking 5 times' and 'each active Spirit now increases your Spirit by 2%'. The cap is five and the HELD stack scales you; the blurb states neither.
digest Soul Feeder (talent:witch-doctor/shadowhunting:13-36-1-3) — 'Increases the damage dealt by Malefic Arrow by 5% for each active Spirit on you.' Direct per-Spirit scaling.
digest Juju Spirits (talent:witch-doctor/voodoo:13-34-10-6) — 'increases the critical strike chance of Bad Juju by 5% for each active Spirit on you.' Direct per-Spirit scaling in the second spec.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE, recorded: structural:witch-doctor/brewing:c-brewing-engine names Cauldron Brewer, Ingredients, Potion Toss and Voodoo Cauldron — and no Spirit at all. No Brewing claim mentions Spirits. The shared engine is real but thinnest at Brewing, so 'each spec runs its own economy on top' is not wholly wrong — it is simply the wrong half to lead with for two specs out of three.

WHY 'corrected' not 'confirmed': the shipped line states only the sustain function ('refund health and mana'). Sustain is true (digest: 'Regenerates ... every 4 sec for 12 sec') but it is the least load-bearing function. The claims show a capped stack that is held for scaling and unleashed for burst. Leading with shared utility while the specs loop on the stack is the Chronomancer failure shape in miniature.

seal_concept.geometry_idea: A carved loa mask sits at the center, and five spirit-wisps hang from a single cord strung beneath it — a fetish necklace, not a ring or an orbit. The wisps brighten left to right toward the fifth, which is the cap and the only one drawn as a crown wisp; the cord's two ends and its low point are where the three spec nodes hang. Every shipped seal so far is a closed figure (eye with orbits, gear grid, ember hexagon, banner between formations, vial in a diamond) — this one is a suspended arc, so the shape itself reads as something held on a string and about to be cut loose.
seal_concept.node_extras: Layer tags on the three nodes, matching the Witch Hunter pattern rather than Guardian's numeric meters: Voodoo = THREADS, Shadowhunting = HUNGER, Brewing = CAULDRON. Proposed center sub-line: EVERY HELD SPIRIT PAYS (traces to Loa Spirits +2% Spirit per active Spirit, Soul Feeder +5% per Spirit, Juju Spirits +5% Bad Juju crit per Spirit). Note: 'INGREDIENTS' was rejected as Brewing's tag — at 11 characters it overruns the longest shipped tag, DAWN·DUSK at 9.

flags: ENGINE WEIGHTING CORRECTED, not the engine name. The shipped blurb 'Collected Spirits refund health and mana; each spec runs its own economy on top' names the right resource but states only its sustain function and frames the specs as running economies beside it. Two of three specs loop directly ON the Spirit stack (Shadowhunting collects with Reclamation and unleashes with Spirit Eclipse; Voodoo collects from damage, Shadow Puppets and Hexfire). Recommend the correction; the sustain fact survives in the body sentence.

DIGEST SELF-CONFLICT — Puppeteer's Threads stores 15% of damage in the class skill entry (spell:witch-doctor:500052) but 10% in the Voodoo talent node (talent:witch-doctor/voodoo:13-34-10-0). I used 10%, since the claim c-voodoo-engine cites the talent locator. If the page prints a percentage at all, this needs resolving first; the strip copy I propose avoids the percentage and uses only the 10-second duration, which both entries agree on.

DIGEST SELF-CONFLICT — Voodoo Hunger gains a stack every 0.5 sec in the class skill entry (spell:witch-doctor:705942) but every 1 sec in the talent node (talent:witch-doctor/shadowhunting:13-36-6-5). I used neither interval; only the 10-stack cap and 10%-per-stack figures, which agree.

DIGEST SELF-CONFLICT — the flat Spirit regeneration amount is '2+ health and mana' in the class skill entries and '7 health and mana' in every talent node. I used neither number; the page should not print the flat amount. The 4-second interval, 12-second duration and 5-stack cap agree everywhere and are safe.

BREWING'S TIE TO THE ENGINE IS THIN. No Brewing claim names Spirits at all — c-brewing-engine, c-brewing-rhythm, c-brewing-role, c-brewing-setup and c-brewing-range all name Ingredients, Cauldron, Potion Toss, Splash Potion, Loa's Brew and Mojo Beam. The digest does supply a link (Spirit Out Of The Bottle, talent:witch-doctor/brewing:13-35-2-5a, grants a Spirit; Spirit Healer, 13-35-10-2, converts the Spirit stat into healing power), but it is one optional node. My seal, verb, gloss, bullets and strip for Brewing therefore rest on Ingredients and the Cauldron, never on spending Spirits. The seal must not imply Brewing unleashes the stack.

NAME COLLISION HAZARD — 'Spirit' is simultaneously the collectible stack and the character stat (Loa Spirits: 'each active Spirit now increases your Spirit by 2%'). Every downstream line must disambiguate. I deliberately avoided writing 'raises your Spirit' anywhere and used the direct per-Spirit riders (5% Bad Juju crit, 5% Malefic Arrow damage) instead of the two-step stat chain.

OPTIONAL TALENTS USED, FLAGGED — A Price To Pay (5-Spirit rider), Soul Feeder (5% per Spirit) and Juju Spirits (5% Bad Juju crit per Spirit) are all SpendCircle/SpendSquare nodes, not guaranteed kit, and no claim names any of them. They are digest-sourced, which the honesty rule permits, but they are build-dependent. If the design pass wants claim-only strips, drop the third Voodoo bullet and the third Shadowhunting bullet.

CONSUMPTION NOT PROVEN — neither the claims nor the digest state that Spirit Eclipse consumes the stack. c-shadow-engine and the digest both say 'unleashes' and 'each Spirit explodes on impact'. Frenzied Spirits (talent:witch-doctor/shadowhunting:13-36-4-9) explicitly 'Consumes your Spirits', which supports but does not prove it for Eclipse. All my copy says 'unleashes', never 'spends' or 'consumes'. The corrected blurb line likewise says 'unleash the whole stack'.

CONTRADICTORY PLAYER-EXPERIENCE CLAIMS FOR BREWING — c-brewing-difficulty (Build Hub: 'not easy') versus c-brewing-easy (reddit: 'among easy healer choices'). Neither is used in any proposal, and no difficulty statement should reach the page from this packet.

NEGATIVE FEEL CLAIM FOR VOODOO, UNUSED — c-voodoo-feel: one current player calls it 'slow and clunky compared with Shadowhunting'. Not used, but it argues against any copy that sells Voodoo as fast or fluid. My verb 'Snap' and the bank topology deliberately sell it as deliberate and stored, which is consistent with both the mechanics claims and this impression.

LIVE-BALANCE CLAIM DELIBERATELY UNUSED — c-brewing-change records an Aug. 7 changelog entry raising Brewing PVE healing 20 percent. That is tuning, not engine shape, and it would date the page. Excluded.

QUARANTINE CHECK CLEAN — no Witch Doctor picker dimension is quarantined, and nothing here rests on chronomancer/artificer, runemaster/riftblade or starcaller/moon-priest evidence. Adjacent-risk note: Brewing's roster range 'Hybrid' and Shadowhunting's 'Ranged' are picker-dimension values, and I did not use them as evidence — the range language in my Brewing bullets comes from c-brewing-range's structural text ('a placed Voodoo Cauldron area with targeted Potion Toss healing'), and Shadowhunting's mobility from c-shadow-range and the Reclamation node.

FIT-CLAIM PROVENANCE — the verb 'Gather' echoes wording in c-shadow-enjoy ('Spirit gathering'), which is a fit statement whose own limitations field reads 'This is a fit statement derived from the listed mechanics.' The verb's actual grounding is c-shadow-engine and the Reclamation node; I cite the mechanics claim, not the fit claim, in the strip.

VERB ALTERNATE FOR BREWING — I chose 'Mix' over 'Brew'. 'Brew' is the literal digest word ('crafting a brew') but restates the spec name and carries no relational information. 'Mix' says what the player does to the engine. Flagging the choice as a judgement call rather than an evidence finding.

TOPOLOGY JUDGEMENT — Shadowhunting is filed 'dual-climb' because c-shadow-tracking explicitly names two changing values (Spirits and Voodoo Hunger). It differs from Inquisition's dual-climb in one important way: the two counts do NOT cash together at a joint gate — Spirits feed Spirit Eclipse, Hunger feeds Malefic Arrow. If the strip vocabulary needs the distinction, a new family name such as 'split-bank' would be more honest than reusing dual-climb.
